rows.stem:
Example of thermal decomposition reaction are

(i) \(\mathrm{2\,AgCl \rightarrow 2\,Ag + Cl_2}\)

(ii) \(\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}\)

(iii) \(\mathrm{2\,H_2O \rightarrow 2\,H_2 + O_2}\)

(iv) \(\mathrm{2\,KClO_3 \rightarrow 2\,KCl + 3\,O_2}\)
rows.solution:
A thermal decomposition reaction is one in which a substance breaks down on heating.

(ii) Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, and (iv) potassium chlorate decomposes on heating into potassium chloride and oxygen: both are thermal decompositions. (i) Silver chloride decomposes in sunlight (photolytic decomposition), and (iii) water decomposes when an electric current is passed through it (electrolytic decomposition).

This is option (D) (ii) and (iv).

rows.stem: Which one of the following metals is protected from corrosion by a layer of its own oxide ?
rows.solution:
Aluminium reacts with oxygen to form a thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide on its surface. This layer sticks firmly to the metal and protects it from further corrosion (the basis of anodising). Copper, silver and gold do not depend on such a layer.

This is option (A) Aluminium.

rows.stem: Electrical impulse travels in a neuron from

options.label: A
options.text: Nerve ending \(\rightarrow\) Axon \(\rightarrow\) Cell body \(\rightarrow\) Dendrite

options.label: B
options.text: Dendrite \(\rightarrow\) Cell body \(\rightarrow\) Axon \(\rightarrow\) Nerve ending

options.label: C
options.text: Cell body \(\rightarrow\) Dendrite \(\rightarrow\) Axon \(\rightarrow\) Nerve ending

options.label: D
options.text: Dendrite \(\rightarrow\) Axon \(\rightarrow\) Nerve ending \(\rightarrow\) Cell body

rows.solution:
An impulse is picked up at the dendrite tip, travels from the dendrite to the cell body, then along the axon to its end, the nerve ending, where it is passed on to the next cell.

This is option (B) Dendrite \(\rightarrow\) Cell body \(\rightarrow\) Axon \(\rightarrow\) Nerve ending.

rows.stem: Which one of the following is **not** an excretory product in plants ?
rows.solution:
Plants get rid of wastes as carbon dioxide (from respiration), as resins and gums stored in old xylem, and through dead cells and falling leaves. Starch is not a waste: it is the food that plants store.

This is option (B) Starch.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The curvature of eye lens of human eye

options.label: D
options.text: increases or decreases as the case may be.

rows.solution:
The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, so its focal length can be adjusted (accommodation). For a nearby object the lens becomes thicker (curvature increases); for a distant object it becomes thinner (curvature decreases).

This is option (D) increases or decreases as the case may be.

rows.stem: In the following groups of wastes, which group contains only non-biodegradable wastes ?

options.label: A
options.text: Leather footwear, Plastic plate, Polythene bag

options.label: B
options.text: Empty medicine bottle, Milk packet, Aluminium can

options.label: C
options.text: Used tea leaves, Cardboard box, Iron nail

options.label: D
options.text: Plastic Syringes, Newspaper, Ball point pen

rows.solution:
Glass bottles, plastic milk packets and aluminium cans are not broken down by decomposers, so all three are non-biodegradable. Each of the other groups contains a biodegradable item: leather footwear, used tea leaves and cardboard, and newspaper.

This is option (B) Empty medicine bottle, Milk packet, Aluminium can.

rows.stem:
Name a metal found in the earth’s crust

(i) in free state and

(ii) in the form of its compound.

State where each of these metals are placed in the reactivity series of metals.
rows.solution:
(i) A metal found in the free state: gold (or silver, platinum, copper). Such metals are the least reactive and lie at the bottom of the reactivity series.

(ii) A metal found in the form of its compounds: sodium (or potassium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium). These very reactive metals lie at the top of the reactivity series. (Metals of moderate reactivity such as zinc, iron or lead, found mainly as oxides, sulphides or carbonates, lie in the middle of the series; this is also acceptable.)

rows.stem: Write the percentage of the energy of sunlight captured by green plants, to convert it into food energy. Explain the fate of this energy when green plants are eaten by primary consumers.
rows.solution:
Green plants capture about 1% of the energy of the sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.

When green plants are eaten by primary consumers, a large part of this energy is lost as heat to the environment, and some is used up in digestion, growth and reproduction of the consumers. On average only about 10% of the food eaten is turned into the consumer's own body and becomes available to the next trophic level.

rows.stem: Explain why respiration is considered as an exothermic reaction. Give the chemical equation for this reaction.
rows.solution:
Respiration is an exothermic reaction because energy is released during the process: glucose in the cells combines with oxygen and gives carbon dioxide and water, and the energy given out keeps the body working.

\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6(aq) + 6O_2(g) \rightarrow 6CO_2(g) + 6H_2O(l)}\) + energy

rows.stem:
(a) “In human beings the genes inherited from the parents decide whether the newborn individual is male or female.”

Explain this statement with the help of a flow diagram.

(b) “Some animals rely on environmental cues for sex determination.” Justify this statement giving an example.
rows.solution:
(a) In human beings the mother has a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, XX, while the father has a mismatched pair, XY. So all the eggs carry an X chromosome, while half the sperms carry X and half carry Y. The sex of the child depends on which sperm fertilises the egg.

Flow diagram:

Male (XY) gives sperms X and Y; Female (XX) gives eggs X.

Sperm X + egg X \(\rightarrow\) zygote XX \(\rightarrow\) girl.

Sperm Y + egg X \(\rightarrow\) zygote XY \(\rightarrow\) boy.

So a child who inherits an X chromosome from the father is a girl, and one who inherits a Y chromosome from the father is a boy.

(b) In some animals sex is not decided by genes. In a few reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept determines whether the animals developing in the eggs become male or female. (In other animals, such as snails, individuals can change sex.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
A person uses lenses of power \(-0.5\) D in his spectacles for the correction of his vision.

(a) Name the defect of vision the person is suffering from.

(b) List two causes of this defect.

(c) Determine the focal length of the lenses used in the spectacles.
rows.solution:
(a) A lens of negative power is a concave (diverging) lens, which is used to correct myopia (near-sightedness).

(b) Two causes: excessive curvature of the eye lens, and elongation of the eyeball.

(c) \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-0{\cdot}5} = -2\) m (\(-200\) cm). The negative sign shows that the lens is concave.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the method by which Amoeba and Leishmania reproduce. Write a major difference in the way they divide to produce new individuals.

(b) What is asexual reproduction ? Explain the process of budding in Hydra.

(c) Give two methods used to grow rose and jasmine plants by vegetative propagation.
rows.solution:
(a) Both *Amoeba* and *Leishmania* reproduce by binary fission. In *Amoeba* the cell can split into two halves in any plane, while in *Leishmania*, which has a whip-like structure at one end, the division occurs in a definite orientation in relation to its structure.

(b) Asexual reproduction is the production of new organisms from a single parent, without the involvement of sex cells (gametes).

Budding in *Hydra*: a bud develops as an outgrowth because of repeated cell division at one specific site. The bud grows into a tiny individual, and when it matures it detaches from the parent body and becomes a new independent individual.

(c) Rose and jasmine are grown by layering and grafting.

rows.stem:
(a) Write one function each of the parts – (i) petals (ii) anther (iii) style and (iv) ovary of a bisexual flower.

(b) Give one example each of a unisexual flower and a bisexual flower. Mention the changes which a flower undergoes after fertilization.
Name the movement which causes ‘X’ and ‘Y’ to grow downwards and upwards respectively.
rows.context: The growth movements of plant parts in which the direction of the stimulus determines the direction of the response is known as tropic movements or tropism. Plants also have non-directional movements which may not be growth dependent.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a potted plant lying on its side, its roots (labelled X) emerging from the pot and bending down, its shoot (labelled Y) curving upwards; the labels X and Y are defined only in the drawing. Page idx 28.
rows.solution: The movement is geotropism, growth in response to gravity. X (the roots) grows downwards, towards gravity: positive geotropism. Y (the shoot) grows upwards, away from gravity: negative geotropism. (The same movements are also described as negative and positive phototropism respectively.)
